alex: Heads-up — enabling FP8 on H100/L40S for the latest rollout is causing short-lived 200–400ms tail spikes on inference (seen in canary). Root looks like kernel fallback + KV eviction churn during calibration windows. Repro steps below.

mike: saw that in telemetry too. spikes correlate with model warmup windows and a small fraction of requests hitting an INT8 slowpath.

sophia: any error logs from the runtime? can you paste the kernel selector trace?

alex: pasted below — this is a 10s sample around the spike. note the repeated fallback reason: "quant_calib_mismatch" and then immediate KV cache eviction events.

alex: ```
2026-03-16T15:12:03Z kernel_select: model=redwood-13b-fp8 target=H100 config_flags=fp8_enabled=true
2026-03-16T15:12:03Z kernel_select: chosen=te_fp8_dotprod v=1.2 latency_est=3.4ms
2026-03-16T15:12:04Z kernel_select: chosen=te_fp8_dotprod v=1.2 latency_est=3.6ms
2026-03-16T15:12:04Z kernel_select: fallback=nvfuser_int8 v=0.9 reason=quant_calib_mismatch
2026-03-16T15:12:04Z kv_cache: evict key=conv_cache.size=12->9 reason=hotpath_backpressure
2026-03-16T15:12:04Z runtime_trace: perf_counters{warp_stalls=120,mem_bandwidth=840GB/s}
2026-03-16T15:12:05Z kernel_select: chosen=te_fp8_dotprod v=1.2 latency_est=3.5ms
2026-03-16T15:12:05Z kernel_select: fallback=nvfuser_int8 reason=quant_calib_mismatch
2026-03-16T15:12:05Z kv_cache: evict key=kv::session-42 reason=eviction_threshold_exceeded
```

mike: interesting — fallback reason is not thermal or OOM, it's specifically quant calibration disagreement. my guess: streaming calibration step (on first few tokens) produces a distribution that trips the FP8 confidence heuristic and we revert to int8 path which has higher per-token latency and different memory layout -> causes extra KV writes and evictions.

sophia: can we confirm the calibration window size and whether it's tied to batchshape? also curious if batching heuristics amplify this: a 1->4 microbatch ramp might spike occupancy and cause kernel probe to re-evaluate.

alex: checks below — the canary config: batch_target=16, microbatch=1->4 ramp, calib_samples=64 (auto). When requests arrive with long context and varied tokenization we see the runtime re-evaluate kernels mid-stream.

alex: quick diff of the selector heuristics I ran locally: ```
- if fp8 && fidelity_score>0.8 then choose te_fp8
+ if fp8 && fidelity_score>0.85 && stable_distribution then choose te_fp8
```

perf-bot: perf-alert: 03/16 15:12: spike detected on canary-group-2: p99 latency increased from 24ms -> 280ms for 0.3% of requests. linked traces: https://perf.internal/reports/3123456789

mike: two actionable hypotheses: 1) calibration heuristic too aggressive during mixed microbatch ramp; 2) KV eviction threshold too low when path switches cause temporary memory layout churn. both could cause the tail spikes.

sophia: +1. propose short-term mitigations: a) disable on-the-fly kernel re-eval for requests that have started (prevent mid-request fallback), b) bump kv_cache.eviction_threshold by 25% for canaries, c) log raw calibration stats to correlate fidelity_score and token distributions.

alex: implemented a quick toggle to prevent mid-request re-eval in the selector and rolled to canary. also increased eviction_threshold to 1.25x for the canary pool. initial 5m looks promising (p99 back to ~30ms). will let it run for an hour.

deploy-bot: rollout: selector-lock-toggle=true rolled to canary-group-2 at 15:28 by alex :rocket:

mike: for longer-term fix we should: - adjust fidelity thresholds per-model and per-hw (H100/L40S diffs) - add a warmup path that pins kernel selection for the first N tokens to avoid oscillation - expose a telemetry metric: kernel_handoff_rate per-second so we can alert on bursts.

sophia: also considering a small bounded grace-period for KV eviction after handoff events (e.g., delay eviction decisions for 100ms after kernel route change). that should prevent immediate thrash.

alex: agreed. I'll open a PR with: kernel_handoff_rate metric, selector stability tuning per device, and kv eviction grace window. tracking in issue: https://go/repo/issue/INF-8492

perf-bot: perf-update: 15:36 canary p99=32ms, spikes suppressed. continuing observation. :white_check_mark:
